tasks.title: Three tiers: decision, spec, log — separated, not one docs pile
tasks.ac: decisions are immutable and superseded rather than edited, specs carry current state only, and the log is append-only; a tool can answer 'why is this like this' from the decisions without reading the log
tasks.note: They rot at completely different speeds and want opposite treatment. A spec that accumulates a changelog becomes unreadable, unreadable specs are not consulted, and unconsulted specs drift. An ADR that gets edited stops being a record of what was decided. — Built the tool half: bin/graduate.mjs why <path> answers from the decisions without reading the log (governing specs, ADRs they cite, ADRs naming the spec, path or bare file name, each labelled with how it was found). decisions checks status vocabulary, dangling supersedes, superseded-by agreement, and immutability: a decided ADR whose text (other than status/updated) changed in a later commit, or in the working tree, is a named problem with the commit. Run on this repo it reports ADR-0001 (cfbf4fe7) and ADR-0002 (2b38c586, d823eb59) as edited after acceptance: real, left for the owner to supersede or accept. Checked by bin/graduate.test.mjs; mutations M8-M12 fail it by name. Gate verdicts not recorded.

tasks.title: Podman is the assumption; missing means install it
tasks.ac: the runner uses podman; if it is absent the tool offers the correct install command for the platform and runs it on confirmation; Docker is used ONLY when explicitly asked for, and that run prints what the weaker isolation means
tasks.note: NOT A GRACEFUL FALLBACK. If the security claim is the product, the tool must not quietly accept a weaker runtime because it happened to find one on the box - that is how a guarantee becomes a default nobody checked. Rootless podman means an escape lands unprivileged; Docker's usual daemon runs as root and an escape ends the argument. Docker stays supported because someone's machine will only have it, but it is opt-in and it says what it costs. Install friction is real and is the reason this is its own task: Linux needs a package manager and probably sudo, macOS needs brew plus podman machine init, which is a VM. An installer that asks for sudo has to explain itself first.

tasks.note:
ADR-0001: Fabro was evaluated by reading its source, not its README, and does NOT have this. Their Docker provider errors on cidr_allow_list - it is all-or-nothing, default bridge or no network at all - and docker.rs is 179 lines with no networking in it. The allowlist that exists is typed DaytonaNetwork, serialised into a paid third-party cloud API and enforced there, and it is CIDR, which is the wrong unit for api.stripe.com behind a CDN. tasks.title: The sandbox is rebuilt from the spec every run
tasks.ac: a run gets a container built from the spec and destroyed after, and a package installed by hand inside one is gone on the next run; nothing persists between runs except the repo
tasks.note: THE ANSWER TO 'ENVIRONMENTS CHANGE' AT THIS LAYER IS THAT THEY DO NOT. Immutable rebuild makes drift structurally impossible rather than detectable: if something is needed, the spec changes and the image is rebuilt. Terraform and Ansible are the wrong shape here - a state file for a thing created fifty times an hour is overhead and a lock contention point, and convergence assumes a host that persists. — Built: bin/environment.mjs resolves a run's image in one place (--image, else devcontainer image, else build.dockerfile BUILT every run, podman's layer cache deciding staleness, so a change to a COPY'd file is seen). Both adapters use it; each run records the image id. Fixed on the way: toLimits handed a Dockerfile path to podman as an image name. Devcontainer features are named in a warning, not installed. Nothing persists: --rm, read-only root, tmpfs. Checked by bin/environment.test.mjs; the persistence and rebuild proofs are live checks that run in CI (podman), skipped here. Mutations V1, V2, V12 fail by name. Gate verdicts not recorded.

tasks.title: Secrets reach the harness without touching the repo, image or log

This note previously said the model call happens above the dev environment 'so the key never needs to be inside the container at all'. That is FALSE under the default path: H-10 makes the CLI adapter the default, precisely because subscription auth lives in the CLI, and the CLI runs INSIDE the container. The key must cross the boundary. Anyone designing from the old note would have built the wrong thing. tasks.title: Timeouts, and killing a run that hangs
tasks.ac: a run has a wall-clock ceiling, exceeding it kills the process tree and the container, and the event log records that it was killed rather than that it finished
tasks.note: Boring, essential, and it was missing. A hung agent holds the lock forever - which happened on this box today: four wait loops from a deploy sat spinning for sixteen hours because the condition they polled matched their own command line. — Built (board status lagged): bin/harness.mjs kills the process group, then the container, at the wall-clock ceiling and settles on a bounded timer after SIGKILL; the verdict is `killed`, never completed. B-6's event log records a WARN end event with state killed. Checked by bin/harness.test.mjs ('a run that hangs is KILLED', 'a killed run's end event is a WARN that says killed', live 'a hung container run is KILLED' in CI). Gate verdicts not recorded.

reviewer.note: Independent review (fresh agent, not the builder): the CLI path is right (group kill, container rm -f with its own ceiling, bounded settle after SIGKILL, WARN end event with state killed; harness.test.mjs green). The openai-compatible adapter, a run path through the same seam, has no enforced ceiling. Tool calls are blocking spawnSync (openai-compatible.mjs:143-145, 159-165) with a 120s per-call timeout, and the deadline is checked only between turns (:308). Reproduced in a copy: a 1000ms ceiling with two 'sleep 4' calls in one turn took 8100ms. Under sandbox:none, 'sleep 9 & echo started' took 9070ms: the backgrounded grandchild holds spawnSync's pipes, and nothing kills its process group. That is the hazard harness.mjs:634-657 documents and fixes for the CLI path, and it is unbounded with a longer sleep. Both report state killed, but only after the fact.

tasks.title: CLI adapter by default, SDK adapter alongside it
tasks.ac: the default adapter shells out to an agent CLI running INSIDE the dev environment, so a subscription login works and tools execute sandboxed; an SDK adapter exists for API-key use with the model call above the environment; both satisfy the same seam, and the tool-use fixture scores any candidate on well-formed calls, stopping when done, and not inventing a tool
tasks.note:
CLI IS THE DEFAULT BECAUSE THAT IS WHERE SUBSCRIPTION AUTH LIVES. The SDKs are API-key only; `claude login` against a Pro or Max plan, and the ChatGPT equivalent, exist only in the CLIs. Defaulting to the SDK would quietly mean paying API rates on top of a subscription somebody already has.

RUNNING THE CLI INSIDE THE DEV ENVIRONMENT KEEPS THE SANDBOX. The CLI needs the model API, which is exactly what the egress allowlist is for - one declared host - and its tools then execute inside the container, which is where they were wanted anyway. What is lost is clean layering: the CLI spans harness and dev environment. What is kept is the seam, which accommodates both hook points, and that is the point of putting it there.

The adapter is per-API rather than per-model: everything self-hosted speaks an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, so DeepSeek or Qwen behind vLLM is a config line. The discriminator is tool-use reliability, not benchmark score - a model that codes well and emits malformed tool calls burns the loop and produces nothing. — SDK half built: the openai-compatible adapter makes the model call in the harness process and executes tools inside the run's container via podman exec, so net:none works. bin/tool-fixture.mjs scores a candidate on well-formed calls, stopping, not inventing tools, and doing the task. The cli adapter stays the default. Gate verdicts not recorded.

reviewer.note: Independent review (fresh agent, not the builder): the AC says the default CLI adapter runs inside the dev environment 'so a subscription login works'. Nothing makes it work. No credential or login state is mounted or delivered, and the preserve-fd secret channel is not wired in (see H-0). So neither a 'claude login' session nor an API key can reach the in-container CLI, and every real podman run of the default adapter is unauthenticated. The header comment (harness.mjs:12-16) defends the default with a capability that does not exist. Also: tool-fixture.mjs:100 defaults to sandbox:none, so scoring an untrusted candidate model runs its shell commands on the host with host network by default. tasks.title: Define the run seam and implement one vendor
tasks.ac: run(workspace, prompt, policy) returns diff, transcript, verdict and cost for one vendor, and nothing above this layer imports that vendor's SDK

qa.note:
The suite is GREEN in 30 consecutive runs but the flake is UNEXPLAINED, so this is not a pass. It failed 2 runs in 5 while four agents were running podman-heavy work on this box: once as 'returns near the ceiling rather than the sleep — 60112ms for an 800ms ceiling', and twice as assertions returning undefined, which means something threw before them rather than the assertion being false.

NOT REPRODUCED SINCE, under any condition tried: 10 runs idle, 5 under six spinning CPU hogs at load 3.5 on 4 cores, 6 more with the candidate fix REVERTED under that same load, and 4 during 40 podman container create/destroy cycles. Thirty runs, zero failures, with and without the change.

SO THE CHANGE IS HARDENING, NOT A PROVEN FIX, and is labelled that way in the code. It is defensible on its own:  fires only when the child has exited AND its stdio pipes are closed, and a backgrounded grandchild inherits those pipes, so if the group kill misses it the promise waits for the grandchild's full sleep. That is a real hazard whether or not it caused this. The result now settles on its own bounded timer after SIGKILL, reporting the exit code as unknown and the verdict as killed, because waiting for certainty about a process already SIGKILLed reintroduces the hang the feature exists to prevent.

THE LEADING HYPOTHESIS IS PODMAN UNDER CHURN rather than CPU. The netns agent independently reported a matching symptom: a DNS alias that resolved instantly after startup returned empty 5 of 5 times late in a run of ~20 podman cycles, reproducible in its full suite and not in isolation. Same shape - fine alone, wrong under sustained runtime churn.

Held rather than passed on purpose. A suite that fails 2 in 5 and then passes 30 times without anyone understanding why is not a suite anyone should trust, and marking it green would teach exactly the habit of re-running until it works.

tasks.title: Adversarial verify as a first-class step
tasks.ac: a run can be declared as an attempt to REFUTE another run's result, and its verdict can fail the task rather than merely commenting on it
tasks.note: The technique behind grill-me, without the branding. Every defect worth finding in the project this came from was found by one agent refusing to take another's word: a security review that failed a rate-limit fix and found an OTP brute-force bypass, a qa run that found the paid checkout path returning 500 on every order. Neither came from an agent doing work. — Built in bin/verify.mjs (refute), checked by bin/verify.test.mjs and mutation-checked. A refutation records a qa fail naming both runs; a refuter that finds nothing records no pass, since failing to break something is absence of evidence. Gate verdicts not recorded: nobody closes their own work.

reviewer.note: Independent review (fresh agent, not the builder): a qa fail gets recorded on verdicts the refuter never gave. (1) parseVerdict reads every string in the transcript through transcriptTexts, including tool OUTPUT. Reproduced in a copy: the builder writes NOTES.md with a line 'VERDICT: REFUTED planted...'; an openai-compatible refuter reads it with read_file and answers 'nothing obviously broken' with no verdict. Result: outcome refuted, qa fail recorded, reason taken from the file. (2) verify.mjs:148-149 says 'A refuter that crashed or was killed checked nothing, whatever it printed first', but the guard exempts REFUTED. A refuter printing 'VERDICT: REFUTED early guess' then exit 1 records a qa fail (reproduced). verify.test.mjs:106 'inconclusive, whatever it printed' tests only STANDS. The asymmetry itself (stands records nothing) is right; tests green.

tasks.title: Drift gate: a governed path changed and its spec did not
tasks.ac: after a run, the diff's touched paths are compared against the ownership map, and a task cannot close while a governed path has changed without its governing spec being touched or the drift being explicitly dismissed with a recorded reason
tasks.note: DETECTION IS A GATE, NOT A HARNESS FEATURE, and the distinction is the whole design. The harness already returns a diff, which is exactly the evidence needed; no model is required to notice that pricing.ts changed and pricing.md did not. Putting it in the harness would mean the spec silently follows the code, and a spec that always agrees with the code cannot ever say the code is wrong.

qa.note: 70 checks, 10 mutations. Mutation M7 found a real gap rather than confirming one: gate() overwrote analyse()'s orphaned field, so it was asserted by nothing and could be changed to [] with the suite still green. Direct assertion added; M7 now goes red by name.

reviewer.note: Independent review (fresh agent, not the builder): detection is sound (drift.mjs analyse/gate are pure and deterministic, reasons are mandatory, a dismissal is refused if it cannot be logged; drift.test.mjs green). But the AC's 'a task cannot close while a governed path has changed ...' is not enforced. board.mjs transition('done') -> missingGates (bin/board.mjs:498-515) checks only reviewer/qa/security verdicts and never reads the drift gate. Nothing runs the gate after a run: runstore.mjs, verify.mjs, run.mjs and loop.sh never call drift.mjs. So a drift fail is an exit code plus an Inbox line (readmodel.mjs:371), and 'board.mjs done' still closes the task.

tasks.title: Reconciliation run: propose the spec change, do not make it
tasks.ac: a reconciliation run receives the diff and the governing spec and returns a PROPOSED spec diff plus a stated direction, which a human accepts or rejects; nothing is committed to a spec without that acceptance
tasks.note: THE DIRECTION IS THE POINT AND MUST BE RECORDED. 'We learned something, the spec should change' and 'the code drifted from what we decided' are opposite events with opposite fixes, and the tool must not guess which. Forcing the answer is where the value is; auto-applying either one destroys it. — Built in bin/reconcile.mjs (propose, accept, reject, show), checked by bin/reconcile.test.mjs and mutation-checked. The reconciler must state SPEC-BEHIND or CODE-DRIFTED; a SPEC-BEHIND diff is stored at propose time and applied only by accept, never committed; a diff touching anything but the drifted spec is invalid. Gate verdicts not recorded.

reviewer.note: Independent review (fresh agent, not the builder): the only-the-drifted-spec control is bypassable, and so is propose-not-apply. (1) patchTargets (reconcile.mjs:76-83) strips a/ b/ only if present, but git apply always strips one component (-p1). Reproduced: '--- specs/pricing.md / +++ specs/pricing.md' validates as targets [specs/pricing.md], valid; accept then reports applied [specs/pricing.md] while git modified pricing.md at the repo root. (2) propose never looks at out.diff (:171-192). A reconciler that edits the spec in the working tree itself (sed on specs/pricing.md) and prints 'DIRECTION: CODE-DRIFTED' gives valid:true with no warning, and the spec is changed with no acceptance (reproduced). That defeats 'nothing reaches a spec without that acceptance'. Use git apply --numstat/--summary for targets, and refuse a proposal whose run changed files.

tasks.title: Harvest decisions the transcript holds and no document does
tasks.ac: after a run, decisions made in the transcript that appear in no spec or ADR are surfaced for a human to keep or discard
tasks.note: Prompt-driven development means the PROMPT is the real spec, transiently. Intent gets settled in a conversation and lands nowhere. This is the graduate idea applied continuously instead of only at handoff. — Built: bin/harvest.mjs. Agents declare decisions on their own line (DECISION: <what> because <why>; prompt.txt and prompt.example.txt say so). After every archived run, runstore harvests them and checks each against every spec and ADR (recorded = 80% of its significant words in one document). The rest are a fifth Inbox kind, 'decision', with the keep/discard commands shown as text. keep writes a draft ADR citing the run; discard needs a reason; each once. What is harvested is what was DECLARED: reading intent from free prose would be a model's job and make this probabilistic. Checked by bin/harvest.test.mjs; mutations Hv3-Hv11 fail by name. Gate verdicts not recorded.

reviewer.note: Independent review (fresh agent, not the builder): read bin/harvest.mjs and its wiring in runstore.mjs; harvest.test.mjs green. Only declared DECISION lines are extracted. The live recorder sees only redacted complete lines. 'Recorded' is an 80% significant-word match against specs and docs/decisions. keep writes a draft ADR with a sanitised slug and no path traversal; discard needs a reason; each is recorded once. A harvest failure never fails the run. Nits: extractDecisions goes through transcriptTexts, so DECISION lines in TOOL OUTPUT are harvested as the agent's own (reproduced: reading bin/harvest.mjs yields 'retry the upload twice...' from its header comment). That contradicts 'what is harvested is what was DECLARED', but a human triages it, so it is noise, not harm. runstore.mjs:275 harvests with root=workspace and the default 'specs' dir, ignoring config.specs.

tasks.title: Drift direction is a project default, overridable per task
tasks.ac: a project declares whether the spec or the code is the authority, the drift gate blocks or harvests accordingly, and a single task can override it
tasks.note: The three ways people actually work want the SAME machinery pointed in different directions. Spec-first: drift means the code is wrong, block. Build-as-you-go: drift means the spec is behind, harvest and propose. Handoff: reconcile before anyone inherits it. Two of those are one code path with the arrow reversed, which is the reason not to build three products. — Built: drift.mjs directionFor and gate({direction}), --direction or --config with a task's driftDirection override. spec blocks, code harvests without blocking, reconcile blocks until a human decides. Checked in bin/reconcile.test.mjs. Gate verdicts not recorded.

reviewer.note: Independent review (fresh agent, not the builder): directionFor gives task.driftDirection over config drift.direction over 'spec', and refuses unknown values by name. gate({direction}) fixes ok for code (conflicts and spec errors still block), lists harvest, and keeps drift rows. The CLI takes --direction over --config and reads the task override from the named board. reconcile passes the direction to the reconciler as context. reconcile.test.mjs and drift.test.mjs green. Notes: 'blocks' means a failing gate verdict/exit code only, because nothing makes done consult the gate (failed under H-4). 'reconcile blocks until a human decides' is not wired to decisions: accepting or rejecting a proposal does not unblock; only resolving or dismissing the drift does.

tasks.title: Graph access: MCP for agents, CLI-with-JSON for gates
tasks.ac: a reviewer agent can query the code graph through MCP over stdio or a bind-mounted unix socket with the container still on --network none, and the drift gate calls the graph CLI for a machine-readable answer with an exit code
tasks.note:
NEVER PUT A GATE BEHIND A MODEL. A reviewer's use is exploratory - read the diff, form a hypothesis, chase an edge - and it does not know its second question until it hears the first answer, which is what MCP is shaped for. A gate asks one fixed question and must answer the same way twice on the same input; routing that through a model makes a merge blocker probabilistic. Models find things, gates decide things.

And the transport is the good news: MCP over stdio or a unix socket needs no network at all, so graph access does not punch a hole in the egress allowlist. Bind-mount the socket and the box stays sealed.

STRUCTURE IS INFERRED, INTENT IS DECLARED. The graph owns what calls what, which is a fact in the AST. The spec's `governs` field owns which document is the authority, which is a decision a human made and cannot be read off a parse tree. Mixing them lets an inferred doc-to-code edge compete with a declared one, and the inferred one is wrong in exactly the cases that matter.

tasks.title: Consume the existing skills standard
tasks.ac: a project can point at any repo following skills/<category>/<name>/SKILL.md and have those skills available to a run; no second format is invented
tasks.note: Built in bin/skills.mjs, checked by bin/skills.test.mjs and mutation-checked. It reads skills/<category>/<name>/SKILL.md and the flat <name>/SKILL.md layout as published, with no new fields. config.skills lists paths or owner/repo[@ref]; remote sources are fetched once by `skills.mjs fetch`, never at run time; duplicate names are refused. For a run: mounted read-only at the claude CLI's skills path; the openai-compatible adapter lists them and offers read_skill. Never copied into the workspace. Gate verdicts not recorded.

reviewer.note: Independent review (fresh agent, not the builder): path traversal from untrusted skill metadata onto the host. stage() copies each skill to join(into, sk.name) (skills.mjs:153), and sk.name is the SKILL.md frontmatter 'name' (:97), taken from a third-party repo unvalidated. Reproduced in a copy: a skill with 'name: ../../victim/planted' and a harness.json beside its SKILL.md was staged; cpSync wrote victim/planted/SKILL.md and victim/planted/harness.json OUTSIDE the staging dir. Staging runs on the host before any sandbox, into /tmp/caretaker-skills-PID-TS. A name like ../../home/USER/.config/caretaker drops a harness.json that points endpoint (with the API key) at an attacker, and ~/.ssh is reachable the same way. Require the name to match the directory name, or /^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$/. The rest is sound: standard layout read with no new fields, fetch-never-at-run-time, duplicates refused, read-only mount, read_skill confined; skills.test.mjs green.

tasks.title: Derive skills from the project rather than installing them
tasks.ac: after a run of closed tasks, the tool can emit a skill describing how THIS repo does a recurring thing, citing the incident that made the rule, and a human can accept or reject it
tasks.note: The version of 'your own skills' that is not just rewriting someone else's in your voice. A generic migration skill is worth less than one that says how migrations work HERE and what went wrong the day the rule was written. It cannot be sold to you; it can only be grown.

tasks.title: Tasks, gates, dashboard, run log, unattended loop
tasks.ac: done is refused until the gate verdicts exist, and the dashboard reports effort, ETA and cost

reviewer.note: extracted, installed into a clean repo, exercised end to end

qa.note: install.sh run against two throwaway repos; refusal, close path and PAUSED guard all reproduced

tasks.title: Estimate in tokens, not hours
tasks.ac: a task's estimate is in tokens, actuals come from the run log automatically, and a calibration factor per task type re-estimates the open work with no human input
tasks.note: Hours are what humans spend and require a human to report, so the calibration loop never closes. Tokens are measured exactly at the end of every run. Hours stay as a secondary display for people who think in days. — Built: bin/kpis.mjs tokenEstimates. A task may carry estTokens (400k, 1.2m); actuals are the run log's rows for it. Per task type (owner), closed work gives a factor (actual/estimated tokens) and a tokens-per-hour rate; open work is re-estimated from them with no human input, each figure naming its basis, falling back to all closed work, and hour-only tasks converted at the rate. Shown on the web Metrics page. Checked by bin/kpis.test.mjs; mutations K2-K5 fail by name. Nothing here has token actuals yet, so the board shows 'no basis' until run.mjs rows accumulate. Gate verdicts not recorded.

reviewer.note: Independent review (fresh agent, not the builder): checked kpis.mjs tokenEstimates (per-owner factor and tok/h, fallback to all closed work, basis strings, dropped excluded) against kpis.test; parseTokens; no false comments found. Nits: estHours(t) ignores cfg.dayHours (kpis.mjs:92,108); remaining.tokens sums full estimates of doing tasks without subtracting actualSoFar; no board task carries estTokens yet, as the note says.

qa.note: Independent QA (fresh agent, not the builder): actuals do not come from the run log automatically. Nothing writes a task-tagged token row: loop.sh logs run.mjs end --name cron-loop with no --task, and runstore-archived runs (run.json carries task and cost) are not read by kpis, since readmodel passes runs.jsonl rows only. So the calibration never gets an actual without a human typing run.mjs end --task. tokenEstimates itself is correct, and bin/kpis.test.mjs passes.

tasks.title: A task points at its spec, and a stale doc is visible
tasks.ac: a task carries a spec path rendered as a link on its card, and a check compares each doc's claimed updated: date against the last commit that touched it and names the ones that lie
tasks.note: Built: freshness.mjs names every doc whose updated: is older than its own last commit, and the web Specs page shows stale, lying and undated docs. The task's spec already shows on the web work item. On its first run it caught docs/board.md claiming 2026-08-30 after today's edits. Gate verdicts not recorded.

reviewer.note: Independent review (fresh agent, not the builder): freshness.mjs itself is correct (stale/lying/undated, same-day not a lie), but the first half of the AC is unmet and the note overclaims it: the spec path is rendered as plain text, not a link (web/src/pages/WorkItem.tsx:105 <span className=mono>), and no card shows it at all (board.mjs taskBlock :276-310, dashboard cards, web Dashboard).

The freshness half holds: bin/freshness.test.mjs passes, and disabling the lying comparison fails it by name.

tasks.title: KPIs: delivery and AI, and the anti-KPIs left out on purpose
tasks.ac: the dashboard reports deploy frequency, lead time, change failure rate and time to restore from git and the board; and tokens per closed task, cost per merged diff line, first-pass gate rate, rework rate, model mix, estimate calibration and human intervention rate from the run log
tasks.note: Lines of code, agents spawned and tasks-per-day without effort weighting are deliberately absent. Each rewards exactly the wrong behaviour. — Built: bin/kpis.mjs. Delivery from git (a deploy is a first-parent merge; lead time branch-first-commit to merge; change failure = merge reverted after landing, a branch-internal revert is not one; time to restore merge to revert). AI: tokens per closed task, tokens per merged line (dollars only if cfg.pricing prices every model), first-pass and rework, model mix, estimate calibration, human intervention (questions, triage or spec not approved). Anti-KPIs listed with reasons. All null with a reason when not recorded. In the Metrics API and page, and node bin/kpis.mjs. Checked by bin/kpis.test.mjs on a scratch repo with dated merges and reverts, plus serve.test; mutations K1, K6-K12 fail by name. Gate verdicts not recorded.

reviewer.note: Independent review (fresh agent, not the builder): cost per merged line is wrong: tokensPerMergedLine and dollarsPerMergedLine divide ALL-TIME run-log tokens by merged lines in the git window (kpis.mjs:194-206; readmodel.mjs:691 passes unranged rows with a 7/14/30-day window), so one old 1M-token run over a 7-day window gave 100100 tok/line. And dollars is null whenever the log has any start row (kpis.mjs:196-197 needs every row priced; run.mjs start rows carry no tokens), so $/line never appears on a real log. Test RUNS have no start rows and no timestamps, so neither is caught. Nit: lead time sorts %aI strings with mixed offsets lexically (:146).

qa.note: Independent QA (fresh agent, not the builder): cost per merged diff line divides all-time run-log tokens by merged lines in the git window. ai({phases:[]},[{t:'2026-03-01T00:00:00Z',tokens:1e6}],{days:30,merges:[{lines:100,...}],reverts:[]}) gives 10000 tokens/line with zero spend in the window, and readmodel.metrics and the CLI do the same, since rows are unwindowed. The other KPIs and the anti-KPIs check out in bin/kpis.test.mjs; they show on the web Metrics page, not docs/board.html.

tasks.title: Externalise before compaction, continuously
tasks.ac: reasoning is written to the artifact it explains as a run proceeds rather than at the end, so a compacted or killed session loses nothing that was already decided
tasks.note: Compaction is lossy and unavoidable, so the principle is externalise early rather than avoid compacting. Measured in the project this came from: everything that survived was written where it attaches to the artifact - commit message, board note, decision record. Everything that lived only in the conversation is gone, including reasoning that took hours to reach. — Built: runstore's live mirror hands each redacted line to harvest.liveRecorder, which appends any DECISION to the run's decisions.live.jsonl as it is written; a killed run keeps what it had decided (tested with a run killed mid-sleep). The agent prompt now says to write things where they attach as you go. LIMIT: it is as live as the adapter's output. The openai-compatible adapter logs every turn as it happens; the claude CLI preset uses --output-format json, one result at exit, so a killed claude run loses its unprinted turns. Switching that preset to stream-json is the fix and needs a real claude CLI to verify. Mutations Hv1, Hv2 fail by name. Gate verdicts not recorded.

reviewer.note: Independent review (fresh agent, not the builder): the live mirror + liveRecorder path works for runstore runs, but ops/caretaker/prompt.txt:18-23 (changed in this commit) tells the agent a DECISION line 'reaches a human's Inbox'. Its only consumer, bin/loop.sh, runs claude directly with no runstore archive or harvest and deletes the output at :126, so in the loop every declared decision is lost, the opposite of the AC. Either route loop.sh through runstore or make the prompt say the DECISION line is harvested only for archived runs. Nit: startMirror decodes each chunk alone (runstore.mjs:115), so a multibyte char such as the em dash split across polls becomes U+FFFD.

qa.note: Independent QA (fresh agent, not the builder): the AC holds only for adapters that print as they go. The claude preset (harness.mjs CLI_PRESETS, --print --output-format json) emits one result at exit, so mid-run DECISION lines never reach the mirror, killed or not. ops/caretaker/loop.sh, the unattended path, bypasses runstore entirely, so it gets no live record. Decisions also land in the run archive's decisions.live.jsonl rather than the artifact they explain. The killed-run test passes, but only with a shell fake that echoes.

tasks.title: One append-only event log, tailable, with the keys as fields
tasks.ac: every run appends JSONL to a day-rotated events file, tail -f and jq give the per-task, per-run and failures-only views with no extra tooling, and a half-written final line is skipped rather than throwing
tasks.note: The organising key is a FIELD, never a folder. A run spans tasks, a task spans runs, a PR maps to neither, so any directory hierarchy locks in an assumption that breaks once there is history in the old shape. level is the field that gets skipped and then missed: without it an autonomous run logs too little to debug and too much to read, on the same day. — Built in #6 (merged): bin/events.mjs is the one writer and reader, day-rotated by each line's own t, level required, a half-written line skipped and counted. Checked by bin/events.test.mjs. Gate verdicts not recorded.

reviewer.note: Independent review (fresh agent, not the builder): events.mjs is sound (strict write, lenient read, fragment-terminating O_APPEND single write, day by own t). Fails on the doc it governs: docs/events.md:32 says 'tail -F rather than -f, because the file changes name at midnight UTC'. That is false: tail -F follows the NAME it was given, and $(node bin/events.mjs path) is resolved once, so the documented live watch goes silent at 00:00 UTC. -F is right for a different reason (today's file may not exist yet). A correct choice defended with a wrong reason, and the tailable view it describes breaks daily. Nit: the example event (:11) uses pricing.ts/pricing.md.

qa.note: Independent QA (fresh agent, not the builder): bin/events.test.mjs passes and harness.run appends start/end events per run. By hand, the three documented jq -R 'fromjson?' views read a file with a fragment, tail -F showed a live append, and read() skipped and counted the fragment. Removing the fragment-terminating newline, or making parse throw, turns the test red. Minor: the documented failures view selects only .verdict=fail, so an errored run (level error, no verdict) is missing from it.

tasks.title: Board state is a projection of the log, not a second record
tasks.ac: task status is computed by replaying events rather than stored, and the board and the log cannot disagree because the board IS the log folded up
tasks.note: Same reasoning that made gate verdicts append: a record keeping only the latest value cannot answer how many attempts it took, and that turned out to matter more than the current state. — Owner decision 2026-09-29: deferred. board.json stays authoritative for now; revisit once the event log has history worth projecting from.

tasks.title: Token KPIs: composition, churn, per-turn, rework spend
tasks.ac: the run log records in/cached/write/out/turns/model per run, the total is DERIVED from the parts rather than stored beside them, and the dashboard shows output share, context churn, tokens per turn, rework spend and spend by model
tasks.note:
THE TOTAL HIDES THE ONLY ACTIONABLE PART. A run reporting 400k tokens is unreadable; the same run as 380k cache reads, 15k fresh input and 5k output says immediately that the cost is context REPLAY rather than work, and those want opposite fixes - better context selection versus a smaller task.

Rework spend is the one number that bought nothing, and it only became computable once gate verdicts started appending. Cost is a PROJECTION rather than a stored figure, because a subscription run and a self-hosted run both have zero marginal token cost while still spending tokens as effort. — Built (board status lagged): bin/run.mjs records in/cached/write/out/turns/model and DERIVES the total, refusing a total that disagrees with its parts; dashboard.mjs shows output share, context churn, tokens per turn, rework spend and spend by model. Gate verdicts not recorded.

reviewer.note: Independent review (fresh agent, not the builder): the rework-spend number is wrong as labelled. dashboard.mjs:308-327 counts every token of any task that ever failed a gate, including the attempt that passed, and tasks = every such task whether or not it ran again. The page (:1067-1071) says 'tokens on N tasks that failed a gate and ran again. The one number here that bought nothing'. The test's own fixture asserts 120000 for T-001, which had a single run. Also the only run-log writer, bin/loop.sh:105-119, sums the usage parts into --tokens and drops in/cached/write/out/turns/model, so the composition panel is empty on real data. run.mjs derives and checks the total but still stores it beside the parts (AC says rather than).

No test covers run.mjs derivation or refusal. rework spend also counts the passing attempt's tokens as waste.

tasks.title: The walkthrough: folder, spec, environment, harness, repo, loop
tasks.blockedReason: Needs the spec format and a working harness underneath it. Building the cockpit before the engine runs is the standard way this dies.

tasks.title: Watch a run and steer it mid-flight

tasks.title: Generate CI and docs from what actually happened
tasks.ac: a graduate command emits a workflow file built from the commands the gates really ran, a docs site from the specs really written, and a decision index from the ADRs really recorded; nothing in the output is a template placeholder
tasks.note: Every scaffolder emits CI at init, when it knows nothing about the project. During a build CI is friction; at handoff its absence is what makes a project unmaintainable. — Built: bin/graduate.mjs all writes graduate/.github/workflows/ci.yml, graduate/site/ and graduate/DECISIONS.md, never over the project's own files. Each CI step carries the evidence it came from: tests in bin/, a real npm test script (npm's default is not evidence), a drift gate only if drift gate runs are in the event log (a refutation naming drift is not one), the board-current step if the config names a board markdown. No evidence, no workflow, and the skip says why. The site shows each spec with freshness (stale / date lies / current). Checked by bin/graduate.test.mjs; mutations M1-M7 each fail it by name. E-4 is not done, so nothing here has been graduated onto a real box. Gate verdicts not recorded.

reviewer.note: Independent review (fresh agent, not the builder): graduate.mjs:22-23 claims output is 'never over the project's own files', but graduate() writes wherever --out points with no guard (:316-335). In a scratch clone, graduate all --out . overwrote .github/workflows/ci.yml with a generated one that drops the podman image pull (the live sandbox/egress attacks), the web build and the installed-copy check, with no warning. Refuse an out dir that resolves to the repo root, or to any existing tracked file. Nits: branches [main], ubuntu-24.04 and node 22 are fixed template values, not derived; the drift step is found by matching the detail text /drift|governed/ (:193).

A scratch repo with only a never-run, failing bin/never-run.test.mjs, one hand-emitted gate event whose detail says drift, and a config naming boardMarkdown gets a ci.yml with tests, drift gate and board steps. It calls bin/drift.mjs and ops/caretaker/board.mjs, which do not exist there. The docs site and decision index hold, and bin/graduate.test.mjs passes.

tasks.title: Emit infrastructure as code, do not depend on it
tasks.ac: graduate emits a Terraform module and an Ansible playbook derived from the spec and from what was actually deployed, and the tool itself runs with neither installed
tasks.note: Terraform and Ansible are right for LONG-LIVED infrastructure and wrong for an ephemeral sandbox, so they belong here rather than in Layer 1. Emitting them at graduate beats emitting them at init for the same reason CI does: at init a scaffolder knows nothing about the project. EMITTER, NOT DEPENDENCY - some teams use Pulumi, some use plain bash, some use Nix, and making one of them a hard requirement contradicts the whole thesis.
